title: Count the stock of every SKU, received or not

blocks.text: A shoe warehouse stocks every shoe as two SKUs, one per foot, and `StockLedger` counts the units on hand. Its pairing report lists the pairs whose left and right counts differ, so that someone goes and finds the missing shoes. Two problems reached the team: the stock report crashes as soon as it is asked about a SKU that hasn't arrived yet, and the big distribution centre's pairing report flags pairs that a manual count found complete.
`report` and `unevenPairs` already work. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/StockLedger.java`:

items: `onHand(sku)`: the units on hand, for any SKU;
`sameStock(a, b)`: whether the two SKUs hold the same number of units, whatever that number is.

cases.says: the report shows the units received per SKU, and a pair whose two small counts differ is flagged
a SKU the warehouse never received reports 0 units instead of failing
two SKUs with the same count of 2,500 units are not flagged as uneven
a SKU registered with 0 units and a SKU never received have the same stock

origin.section: A Wrapper Is an Object: It Can Be null, and == Compares References

concepts: Unboxing a null wrapper throws NullPointerException, as when an absent Map value is assigned to an int.
== on two wrappers compares references; Integer.valueOf is only guaranteed to cache -128 to 127, so equal larger values compare false.
